Y.  ACTION  OF  LIGHT  ox  THE  RETINA. 
That  the  retina  of  certain  animals  was  some 
times  red  had  been  remarked  before,  but  it  was 
discovered  by  Boll  (1876)  that  this  red  colour 
is  bleached  out  by  light,  and  that  it  becomes 
restored  if  the  animal  is  kept  in  the  dark. 
The  green  rays  of  light  are  those  which  are 
most  effective  in  bleaching  out  its  colour, 
corresponding  to  the  fact  that  green  light  is 
most  absorbed  by  a  substance  whose  colour  is 
a  purplish  red.  In  the  human  eye  an  inter 
mediate  stage  in  the  bleaching  out  of  this 
substance  occurs  in  which  it  is  yellow;  and  the 
presence  in  the  retina  of  varying  amounts  of 
the  visual  purple  and  the  visual  yellow  gives
